## 3. Verified source record

The complete JSON entry below is copied from the current local source. Preserve its id, author_id, author_name, day, hour, knowledge_key, timestamp, and exact text. Candidate prose is editorial material, not part of the loaded row.

```json
{
  "id": "journal_raw_b3_04_mechanic_the_hand_crane",
  "text": "Built a hand crane today from the front axle of a tractor and two lengths of the stainless pipe the Mechanic's team brought back from the geo-thermal plant. It lifts the generator fuel drums off the floor so we can roll them instead of dragging them. Dragging was bending the floor plates under the drum cradles. The General came down to look at it and said it was the most useful thing built in the bunker this month. I told him the Botanist built a wheat plant this month. He said wheat plants do not move drums. He is right. The crane does not move drums either, technically. It lifts them. Rolling is what the person does. I am being precise because the General is not precise and someone in this bunker should be.",
  "timestamp": "Day 127, 16h",
  "author_name": "The Mechanic",

}
```

## 4. Fixed canon and open space

A hand crane made from a tractor axle and stainless pipe lifts generator fuel drums so they can be rolled instead of dragged, protecting the floor plates. The General praises it; the Mechanic notes that the crane lifts while a person rolls. The source also mentions a wheat plant built by the Botanist. Do not expand the device into a new operating system or claim it moves drums on its own. Candidate language may add an image, rhythm, or private impression as an editorial draft, but no proposed addition becomes a further remembered event or a confirmed fact until the existing content owner selects and reviews it against the source.

## 5. Human center

The source voice is The Mechanic. The Mechanic’s dry precision corrects the General’s praise without denying the value of the work. Keep the distinction among lifting, rolling, and the person who moves the drum; the joke protects accuracy rather than humiliating anyone. The prose may notice what the author can count, hear, repair, fear, or leave uncertain, while keeping the account’s limits visible.
